verdict: Cloudflare's revenue rose 36% to $696M, but a $151M restructuring charge on top of $141M of stock pay pushed it to a $206M GAAP operating loss and a $170M net loss — even though its non-GAAP operating income was $96M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: basic and diluted, vs -$0.15 a year ago

segments.name: Cloudflare platform
segments.note: One platform: network security, performance and developer services, sold mostly as subscriptions. Cloudflare reports a single operating segment.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform and winning customers; includes $41.246M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes, and $2.391M of amortization of acquired intangible assets.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new products (R&D); includes $55.435M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office (G&A); includes $39.601M of stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes, a $1M legal reserve and settlements charge, and $2.047M of acquisition-related expenses.

opex.name: Restructuring and other charges
opex.note: A one-off restructuring charge taken in the quarter — there was no such charge a year ago. Cloudflare excludes it from its non-GAAP results.

follow100Note: The restructuring charge alone took $21.65 of every $100 Cloudflare took in, and total spending reached $129.55 per $100 — leaving a $24.42 loss per $100 of revenue. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
otherDetail: Interest income of $39.932M, plus $0.913M of other income, net, less $3.089M of interest expense — total non-operating income of $37.756M.
footerNote: Cloudflare reports a single operating segment. GAAP loss from operations was $205.696M; non-GAAP income from operations was $96.1M after adding back stock-based compensation, the restructuring charge and other items listed in the release. Chart note: Cloudflare's running costs exceeded its gross profit; other income covered part of the gap, so the chart draws the remaining $170M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source, which also covers the $2M tax bill.

takeaways.title: Growth re-accelerated
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $696.1M, up 36% YoY, with current remaining performance obligations up 35%. Management pointed to record growth in paying customers, large customers and developers on the platform.

takeaways.title: A restructuring charge drove the loss
takeaways.text: The $150.7M restructuring and other charge — zero a year ago — is the single biggest reason the GAAP operating loss widened from $67M to $206M. Excluding it and stock pay, non-GAAP operating income was $96.1M, a 13.8% margin.

takeaways.title: Stock pay remains the steady gap
takeaways.text: Stock-based compensation and related payroll taxes were $140.6M in the quarter, about 20% of revenue. Free cash flow was still positive at $56.4M, and Cloudflare held $4,162.8M of cash and available-for-sale securities.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other charges of $150.693M were taken in the quarter (none in the year-ago quarter); Cloudflare excludes the charge from its non-GAAP results.
General and administrative costs include a $1M legal reserve and settlements charge and $2.047M of acquisition-related expenses.
